steps.body: Some graphs mirror themselves. A function is **even** if f(−x) = f(x) — the y-axis is a mirror. It's **odd** if f(−x) = −f(x) — a half-turn about the origin lands the graph on itself. The test is **algebraic**: substitute −x and simplify. Whatever comes out decides.
Run the test on a candidate.

widget.prompt: Trace x² to x = −2 and read the height, then compare it with the height at x = +2.
widget.successFeedback: Both give 4. A function is EVEN when f(−x) = f(x) — the graph is its own mirror image across the vertical axis — and x⁴ − 3x² behaves the same way for the same reason: every exponent is even.
widget.lowFeedback: Still to the right of x = −2.

steps.body: One matching pair isn't proof — the test must hold for **every** x. Substitute the letter: f(−x) = (−x)⁴ − 3(−x)² = x⁴ − 3x² = f(x). Every even power survives the sign flip, so any polynomial with **only even powers** is even; only odd powers, odd.

explanationVariants: All powers (3 and 1) are odd, so flipping x flips every term — the whole output negates.

options.label: Even
options.feedback: Even needs g(−x) = g(x), but g(−1) = 2 while g(1) = −2 — outputs flip sign instead. That's odd.

options.label: Neither
options.feedback: It passes the odd test cleanly: g(−x) = −x³ + 3x = −(x³ − 3x). Every term negates together.

explanationVariants: h(−x) = x² − x, which is neither h(x) = x² + x nor −h(x) = −x² − x: neither.
Check a point: h(1) = 2 but h(−1) = 0 — not equal (kills even) and not opposite (kills odd).

options.label: Neither even nor odd
options.feedback: Right — the even-power term keeps its sign while the odd-power term flips, so h(−x) matches neither h(x) nor −h(x).

options.label: Even
options.feedback: h(−1) = 1 − 1 = 0 but h(1) = 2 — unequal outputs at ±1 break the mirror. Mixed even AND odd powers usually give neither.

options.label: Odd
options.feedback: Odd needs h(−1) = −h(1) = −2, but h(−1) = 0. The x² term refuses to flip sign.

explanationVariants: A y-axis mirror is exactly the even condition f(−x) = f(x).
Fold the paper along the y-axis: the halves coincide only when opposite inputs share an output.

widget.prompt: A graph is symmetric about the y-axis. What must be true?

options.label: f(−x) = f(x) for every x — the function is even
options.feedback: Exactly — mirror-image points (x, y) and (−x, y) share the same height.

options.label: f(−x) = −f(x) for every x — the function is odd
options.feedback: That's the ORIGIN (half-turn) symmetry. A y-axis mirror keeps heights equal, not opposite: f(−x) = f(x).

options.label: f(x) ≥ 0 for every x
options.feedback: Mirror symmetry says nothing about sign — y = x² − 5 is even yet dips below zero.

explanationVariants: k(−x) = 5(−x)³·? — compute: 5(−x)⁶ = 5x⁶ and −2(−x)⁴ = −2x⁴ and +7 stays: k(−x) = k(x). Even (a constant is an even term: 7 = 7x⁰).
All exponents present — 6, 4, and 0 — are even, so the sign flip changes nothing.
hints: Substitute −x into every term, including the constant.
(−x)⁶ = x⁶ and (−x)⁴ = x⁴. What about the 7?
7 = 7x⁰, and 0 is an even power — every term survives unchanged, so k(−x) = k(x).

options.label: Even
options.feedback: Right — exponents 6, 4, 0 are all even, so k(−x) = k(x).

options.label: Odd
options.feedback: Odd would need EVERY term to negate; here none do — (−x)⁶ = x⁶, (−x)⁴ = x⁴, and 7 can't flip sign at all.

options.label: Neither, because of the +7
options.feedback: A constant is an even-power term (7x⁰), so it PRESERVES evenness. The +7 would only break ODDNESS.

takeaways: Even: f(−x) = f(x), mirror in the y-axis.
Odd: f(−x) = −f(x), half-turn about the origin.
Test with the letter −x; a single point can only DISPROVE.
steps.teaser: Next: functions built from pieces — different rules on different stretches of x.

concept.body: Substitute −x. Everything unchanged → even. Every term negated → odd. A mix → neither. Polynomials: check whether all exponents are even, all odd, or mixed.

explanationVariants: Only odd exponents (5 and 1), so m(−x) = −m(x): odd.

options.label: Odd
options.feedback: Right — exponents 5 and 1 are both odd; every term flips with x.

options.label: Even
options.feedback: m(1) = 5 but m(−1) = −5 — opposite, not equal. That's the odd pattern.
